subject: SLO discovery: streaming/latency probe plan + prompt delivery
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Montoya <emontoya@fastpay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: SLO discovery: streaming/latency probe plan + prompt delivery

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful session. This thread captures the agreed next steps for performance qualification and the small set of artifacts we need to run a reproducible probe/benchmark. I copied Ben and Kimberly so they can pick up execution and licensing points.

Summary of what we discussed and what we need from FastPay to proceed:
- Targets: p95 latency target = 150ms end-to-end for the sync flow; streaming steady-state target = 150 tokens/sec with tail p99 latency under 600ms per chunk. Please confirm these are still the goals.
- Throughput/Concurrency: target steady QPS range = 60-120 QPS for peak hour; concurrency target for connection-based streaming = up to 400 concurrent connections.
- Representative traffic: we need your 1-hour sample of real traffic or a synthetic profile (CSV) showing request size distribution, token counts, and inter-arrival times. If you prefer private data handling, we can run the probe inside your VPC.
- Prompt sets: you said you could share a trimmed prompt set. Please send the non-PII prompt_set_v3.jsonl (or an anonymized sample) plus a mapping of which prompts map to which SLA buckets.
- Measurement definitions: our measurement will use p95/p99 latency for requests, tokens/sec for streaming throughput, and sustained error rate under 0.1%. We will also report cost per 1M tokens for the tested config.
- Reproducibility: we plan to publish a short runbook and the harness config we used. If you want the run to be private, tell us and we will mark artifacts accordingly.

Attached: initial SLO matrix (slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) and our recommended traffic CSV template. Links: runbook draft in Drive (see link below).

Action items and proposed deadlines:
1) FastPay to deliver prompt_set_v3.jsonl and traffic_profile.csv by Tue 2027-05-18.
2) Redwood to provide a 2-hour probe window and a config file to run in-host or in-VPC by Fri 2027-05-21.
3) Scheduling: suggest Wed 2027-05-26 for a short pre-run check and Thu 2027-05-27 for the main probe window (times TBD based on your ops schedule).

If those dates don't work, propose alternatives. Also let us know if we should route the run under an NDA or your standard data handling agreement.

Best,
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- slo_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- traffic_profile_template.csv (csv)

Runbook draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-fastpay-bench-runbook

From: Elena Montoya <emontoya@fastpay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: sre@fastpay.com
Date: 2027-05-14T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO discovery: streaming/latency probe plan + prompt delivery

Thanks Priyom — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Targets: Confirmed. p95 150ms for the synchronous path. For streaming, the important metric for us is tokens/sec and recovery time after network pauses. The p99 per-chunk under 600ms is acceptable.
- Throughput: our peak user-facing QPS is around 90 right now; we can provision a synthetic load to mimic spikes up to 130 QPS during the run.
- Concurrency: 400 concurrent websocket streams is our upper bound. Not all streams are active simultaneously; expect 60-80% active token emission.
- We attached the anonymized prompt_set_v3.jsonl with a short README and a traffic_profile.csv (1-hour sample, aggregated token counts per minute). The sample is scrubbed for PII.

Logistics questions:
1) We prefer Redwood to run the probe in our staging VPC. Please send the IA and the minimal infra spec for the runner.
2) Security: we have a standard questionnaire and will need an SOC2 artifact before we allow hosted test access. I am looping in procurement separately for the contract items.

We can hit the 2027-05-18 window for prompt delivery — attached. For the pre-run check, Wednesday 2027-05-26 in the morning Pacific works.

Thanks — attaching files now.

Elena
Head of Platform Engineering
FastPay

Attachments:
- prompt_set_v3.jsonl (jsonl)
- traffic_profile.csv (csv)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Montoya <emontoya@fastpay.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO discovery: streaming/latency probe plan + prompt delivery

On Fri, 2027-05-14 at 10:07 AM Elena Montoya <emontoya@fastpay.com> wrote:
> Thanks Priyom — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side: ...

Appreciate the prompt set and traffic sample — that should be enough for an initial probe. Kimberly and Ben, can you confirm run approach below?

Proposed run approach (high level):
- Phase 0: Pre-run validation and data acceptance (confirm sanitized prompts, validate traffic CSV). Estimate 1 day.
- Phase 1: Staging VPC dry-run (non-prod) where we validate harness stability and metric collection. 1 hour run with low offset load.
- Phase 2: Full probe window in staging VPC: 2 x 1-hour runs covering steady-state and spike profile. Collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, error rates, and resource utilization.
- Phase 3: Reproducibility: capture the harness config, seed values, and exact workload generator config. We'll publish those artifacts to the shared Drive folder unless you request marking them private.

Re security: we can attach our SOC2 summary and our minimal infra spec to this thread. If FastPay needs us to run everything inside your VPC, we will need a short runner role and ephemeral credentials. Ben, can you add the runner spec and a checklist for the staging VPC access?

If this looks good, we'll lock in Wed 2027-05-26 for the pre-run check and Thu 2027-05-27 for the main probe.

--
Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Montoya <emontoya@fastpay.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-17T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO discovery: streaming/latency probe plan + prompt delivery

Hi all,

Thanks for the artifacts, Elena. Quick operational notes and what we'll deliver ahead of the pre-run:

Deliverables before Wed 2027-05-26 pre-run:
- Runner infra spec (minimal instance types, network ports, IAM role) - link to drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-fastpay-bench-runbook (we'll add a small README).
- SOC2 summary and minimal data handling note (pdf) - will be attached to the shared folder and also uploaded to the procurement ticket.
- Harness config tarball (harness-config-v1.tar.gz) with seed and workload generator config.
- A sanitized test checklist for VPC onboarding.

Operational asks from FastPay:
- Please whitelist the ephemeral runner public key once we create the role and provide an onboarding window of 2 hours for configuration.
- Confirm which Drive artifacts should be private vs shared.

I'll be your exec contact for the run and will post the run summary to the Drive folder within 24 hours of the probe. If FastPay prefers Redwood to run the probe entirely hosted, we can provide a hosted config as a fallback.

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced:
- harness-config-v1.tar.gz (archive)
- runner_infra_spec.md (doc)

Next: we'll schedule a 30-minute dry-run check on Wed 2027-05-26 09:00 PT unless you propose another time.
